subtopic: Using AI tools for learning without cheating
subtype: Approach: being open with the teacher about use [Action]
passage:
Dear Pema Ma'am,
Before I submit my essay on climate and farming, I wanted to tell you how I used an AI tool. I asked it for five angles I could take, and I picked the one on water use. I also asked it to point out grammar mistakes, and I fixed them myself. All the sentences and arguments are mine, and I have attached my rough notes so you can see how the essay grew. I wasn't sure if this is within the rules for the assignment, so I would like to ask you directly. If any of it is not allowed, I'm happy to change it before you mark it. P.S. I would rather ask now than have you wonder later.
Yours sincerely,
Parveen

qa.q: What did Parveen ask the AI tool to do?
qa.a: Parveen asked it for five angles and to point out grammar mistakes.

qa.q: Why did Parveen write to Pema Ma'am before submitting?
qa.a: Parveen was unsure whether it is within the rules, and feels honest but a little nervous, wanting to keep the teacher's trust.

qa.q: What could Parveen do if Pema Ma'am says part of it is not allowed?
qa.a: Parveen could redo that part without the tool and ask what help is acceptable, as the email offers.

qa.q: How might Pema Ma'am see the email?
qa.a: Pema Ma'am is likely to appreciate the openness, since it is easier to guide a student who says how the tool was used.

grounding: A teen tells the teacher the AI was used to brainstorm ideas and check grammar, shows the notes and asks whether that fits the rules.

subtopic: Using AI tools for learning without cheating
subtype: Approach: being open with the teacher about use [Action]
passage: Noor, you know how everyone's scared to say they used AI? I just told Mrs. Fernandes straight. I'm Ira, remember, the one who can't keep a secret. For the geography project I'd asked an AI for ten possible topics, because my mind was blank. Then I picked one, flood plains in our own city, and wrote everything myself. I used the tool again at the end only to check grammar. Before submitting, I went to her desk with my notebook: the list of ten topics it gave me, my own notes, and the two grammar changes it suggested. I asked, "Is this okay for this assignment?" She read it, nodded, and said brainstorming and grammar were fine, but next time I should mention it in a line at the end. Then she said, "Thank you for asking." Honestly, Noor, it felt so much lighter than hoping nobody would find out.

qa.a: Flood plains in our own city.

qa.q: How did Ira feel after asking Mrs. Fernandes?
qa.a: Ira felt much lighter and relieved, instead of anxiously hoping nobody would find out.

qa.q: What else could Ira do on the next project?
qa.a: Ira could add a short line at the end saying how AI was used, as Mrs. Fernandes asked, without waiting to be questioned.

qa.q: How did Mrs. Fernandes see Ira's openness?
qa.a: Mrs. Fernandes appreciated being asked, thanking Ira and giving clear guidance, which builds trust between them.

grounding: Shows a teen telling the teacher that AI was used to brainstorm and check grammar, showing the notes and asking whether it fits the rules.

subtopic: Using AI tools for learning without cheating
subtype: Approach: being open with the teacher about use [Action]
passage: I was sitting in the front row when Tenzin went up to Rashmi Ma'am's desk after English. She had her notebook open and her essay on top. I heard her say, "Ma'am, before you mark this, I used an AI tool for two things. It gave me some ideas for the outline, and I used it to check spelling. These are my own notes, and this is what it suggested." Rashmi Ma'am read for a minute. Then she tapped one page. "The outline ideas are fine. But this paragraph is very close to what the tool wrote." Tenzin nodded. "Should I rewrite it?" "Yes, by Thursday, in your words." Tenzin walked back looking calm, not upset. I can't know what she was feeling inside, but I noticed Ma'am smiled at her afterwards in a way she doesn't usually smile at anyone.

qa.q: What two things did Tenzin use the AI for?
qa.a: Ideas for the outline and checking spelling.

qa.q: What might Tenzin have been feeling on walking back?
qa.a: Tenzin looked calm rather than upset, perhaps relieved at having been open before the essay was marked.

qa.q: What else could Tenzin do to avoid the close-paragraph problem next time?
qa.a: Tenzin could close the tool before drafting and write from her own notes, so its wording doesn't slip into the essay.

qa.q: How does Rashmi Ma'am see Tenzin's openness?
qa.a: She seems to value it, giving a fair fix instead of a penalty and smiling warmly afterwards.

grounding: Illustrates a teen telling the teacher how she used AI, showing her notes and asking whether it fits the rules, which builds trust.
